correctness.rationale: In each open-and-closed fiber of the diagonal idempotent map, the joint spectral projections f_s are orthogonal and sum to one. The conjugator u=Σ_s f_s d_s has residue one modulo the nilpotent radical and satisfies u d_s=f_s u; empty color blocks do not cause an exception. These identities hold over any commutative base K-algebra with the diagonal fixed. The centralizer in 1+J is 1+J_same; it forces all mixed-color coordinates to vanish and imposes no equations on same-color coordinates. To check the actual equation scheme, decompose any u as (1+a)b with b=1+pr_same(u−1) and a=(u−b)b^(-1) in J_diff, since J_diff J_same⊆J_diff. The factorization and its inverse are polynomial, so 1+a gives a unique representative and identifies the fiber functor with affine space of dimension m(c). This also agrees with the tangent equations: Δ=c(x)−c(y) has a unit coordinate when nonzero, giving exactly one tangent direction, including in characteristic two. The finite-field count is q^m(c); every strict comparable pair, not just the covers, contributes its own coordinate. Expanding the edge factor q+(1−q)1_equal gives the spanning-subgraph expression. Interpolation in the two infinite sets of q and Q recovers the polynomial, and Z_G(Q,v)=Q^κ(E) v^(|P|−κ(E)) T_G(1+Q/v,1+v) recovers Tutte after v=(1−q)/q. The fixed graph factors are known; if needed, |P| and κ(E) are the highest and lowest Q degrees of Z, and |E| is the highest q degree of the color sum for sufficiently many colors. Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were read, not executed; their eight examples and Jacobian tests are finite corroboration only.
